Rookies

200.78–1.32 m tall · 18.98 MB

The player roster. Heights are banded by eye to a 1.32 m ceiling, so they read as a set beside each other.

Champions

201.73–3.89 m tall · 20.18 MB

The house-bot tier. Heights are the source art’s own and deliberately not banded — on a winged mon a “height” is mostly wing.

What a portrait is cropped to. The head is not a fixed offset from the top of a mon — Birdramon’s flame wings and Betamon’s dorsal fin both rise well above their heads — so each crop is framed on the geometry actually weighted to that rig’s head bone plus its descendants, which is what carries ears, horns, jaws and antennae. Thirty-five rigs name that bone (J_head, J_atama, J_kubi, J_neck, and J_haed — a typo in the Greymon rips). Five have no head bone at all, because their head is not a separable part: Hagurumon is one floating gear, DemiDevimon a head with wings bolted on, and the Guardromon pair weight head and chest to a single rigid bone. Those five are anchored by hand; open any portrait to see which rule framed it.

Every sprite fills its own frame. These mons run 0.78 m (Otamamon) to 3.89 m (Birdramon) and their footprints spread further still — Raremon is 4.4 × 5.0 m in plan, Garurumon 5.96 m nose to tail. At one fixed camera scale the rookies would be thumbnails. Nothing is lost: manifest.json carries pxPerMeter for every sprite, so 1 / pxPerMeter restores true relative size. TRUE SCALE shows exactly that.

Two facings, and the sun mirrors with them. Both yaws show the same front — only which half of the frame it lands on changes — so the key light is mirrored rather than rotated, and faces stay lit in both. The geometry is never mirrored: asymmetric mons keep their real handedness. Press F to flip facing, P to flip between body and portrait.

Thumbnails here are 256 px WebP. The deliverables are the 512 px PNGs under digimon_sprites/bottom_right/ and digimon_sprites/bottom_left/, rendered from each mon’s idle pose (bn01 frame 1) with the pose baked into the mesh.
